summary: ACPAssessmentCombined is the Canadian Physiotherapy Assessment of Clinical Performance (ACP) assessment tool used for evaluating physiotherapy students during clinical internships. The assessment is structured around the Canadian Essential Competency Profile for Physiotherapists and is organized by professional roles (Expert, Communicator, Collaborator, Manager, Advocate, Scholarly Practitioner, Professional, Summative Comments). It uses multiple rating scales and comment boxes at midterm and final points, based on observable performance anchored to key competencies. The tool incorporates workflows for input, review, and submission, with defined fields, business rules, roles, and system validations.
purpose: To guide, document, and assess physiotherapy student performance during clinical education placements, enabling faculty and clinical instructors to provide structured feedback and assign grades. It gathers quantitative and qualitative evidence for competencies and supports decision-making regarding student progress, remediation, or distinction.

workflows.name: Assessment Workflow
steps: Student is assigned to a clinical placement.
Instructions and rating anchors are reviewed.
At midterm, assessor observes student and completes rating scales for each Role and section.
Comment boxes used for strengths and improvements.
If concerns, 'Please check' checkboxes are used.
At final, assessment is repeated for same sections.
Assessor completes overall recommendation (Credit, Credit with exception, Credit with reservation, No Credit).
Submission workflow locks form for faculty review.
Faculty assigns final grade based on ACP and recommendation.

business_rules: All rating scales must be completed at midterm and final unless stated as not applicable.
Performance anchors require demonstration of all criteria at a level for scoring.
Areas of distinction require evidence of criteria plus one or more exceptional behaviors.
Students must meet minimum criteria for credit; remediation applies if 'credit with reservation' or 'no credit' is assigned.
Assessor and student ratings are tracked separately; consensus and comment required.
Days absent and extra hours worked must be recorded.
Comments must be factual based on clinical observation.
validations: Client consent and confidentiality must be respected.
Assessment answers must be submitted for all required sections.
Text fields for comments must not be empty if concerns flagged.
calculations: Count and comparison of ratings for midterm and final.
Determination of overall recommendation based on rating scale and comments.
Assessment of days absent and extra hours worked.
conditions: If rating scale item not applicable, reason must be entered in comment.
If student performance below expected level, remediation or 'no credit' recommended.
If 'Performance with Distinction' considered, must meet primary criteria and at least one additional exceptional behavior.
system_behavior: Wizard steps guide assessor through each Role.
Sections appear/disappear based on assessor status and read-only mode.
Submission locks assessment for faculty review.
Error and warning panels display missing/invalid entries.
dependencies: Comment workflow depends on observation and evidence.
Final recommendation depends on completed rating scales and comment review.
exceptions: If missing required answers, wizard step remains incomplete.
If assessor or student cannot be found, error message displayed.
If section not applicable, must be documented in comments.
content_gaps: Does not contain actual rating scale values or completed student sample answers.
No full definitions for Likert anchors (except anchor descriptors summary).
No complete validation error messages or full list of UI behaviors.
No implementation code for database or web service layers.
